name: NJ-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 5 points with a favorable national environment for Democrats
Incumbent Herb Conaway holds a large financial edge: $935K raised and $439K on hand versus $807K cash for McGuire
Prediction markets price Conaway at about 94% to win
Minor-party candidates on the ballot are unlikely to alter the two-way margin
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Conaway: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, a dominant fundraising advantage, and markets pricing him near certain. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Conaway or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Herb Conaway, the Democratic incumbent in New Jersey's 3rd District, seeks another term in a seat his party holds with a five-point partisan lean. He has raised about $935,000 and holds $439,000 in cash, while Republican Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 with barely any cash remaining. No outside groups are active in the race, and no independent or Green candidate has shown meaningful funding.

Prediction markets give Conaway roughly a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the district as competitive. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on fundamentals, which all point the same way: a Democratic-leaning seat, an incumbent with a decisive money advantage, and a heavily outspent challenger.
